title: Quieting the Apollo with a ballad; Ike Quebec and Lockjaw
summary: McRae played "Serenade to a Sleeping Beauty" so softly the house hushed, while Quebec and Davis played the hot tenor choruses.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I come out and talk to the men, "Now give me a better show. A lot of people out there, give me a better show."

And Ben Webster on a Monday afternoon "Serenade to a and I was playing (inaudible) Sleeping Beauty, or something that Edgar Sampson wrote a beautiful thing for Coleman Hawkins years ago -- "Serenade To A Sleeping Beauty".
I was playing this thing. It was so pretty. The band (inaudible) with muted brass. And Ben say, "Can't we" --
Come in there with (inaudible), you know. "Go up and get Ol' Teddy (inaudible)." You didn't hear no noise.
When he opened the door, he couldn't get in the theater. He say the theater was so quiet. I was up there playing, he heard this big tone and I was right up into the mike.
They (inaudible), you know, they know how I play, so they bring the volume up or turn it down. (inaudible) so pretty.
He said to me -- he say, "You the only

tenor player to come in here and shut these people up."
We had them listen to a beautiful ballad. How (inaudible) you do it, you know.
Well Ike Quebec and Eddie Lockjaw, they say (inaudible). "What you do, you let us go out there and play and knock ourselves out."
Because I let them do all the playing, you know. Then I just come down and play my special number and something on the end, you know -- about one or two things, you know.
Take it from the top or something I feature myself on, or something like that.
But I had a tone that was, you know, like -- working with the Selmer so long, I had a tone I developed. I could really master the thing.
And they would say, "Well, man, you go out there with your big tone after we get through playing and kill us," you know.
I say, "No, no, no.
What were they playing?
They were playing tenor.
